definitions.explanation: The act or event of something catching fire or beginning to burn. Can refer to both spontaneous combustion and deliberate ignition.

examples.japanese: {発火|はっか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There is a risk of ignition.

examples.japanese: ⟦バッテリー→バッテリー：04425_batterii⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{発火|はっか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{起|お}きた→起きる：00521_okiru⟧。
examples.english: An accident occurred in which a battery caught fire.

examples.japanese: ⟦{乾燥|かんそう}→乾燥：00184_kansou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{季節|きせつ}→季節：01304_kisetsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{枯|か}れ{葉|は}→枯れ葉：20386_kareha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧{発火|はっか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧だ。
examples.english: In dry seasons, dead leaves can spontaneously combust, so caution is needed.

notes:
Describes the moment when something begins to burn. Often used in safety warnings and accident reports. The verb form {発火|はっか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ means "to catch fire" or "to ignite."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {発火|はっか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to catch fire / to ignite
- ⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧{発火|はっか}: spontaneous combustion
- {発火|はっか}{点|てん}: ignition point / flash point
- {発火|はっか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{原因|げんいん}→原因：01400_genin⟧: cause of ignition
- {発火|はっか}⟦{装置|そうち}→装置：03318_souchi⟧: ignition device
- {発火|はっか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧: risk of catching fire

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {着火|ちゃっか}: ignition — very similar, but often implies intentional lighting; {発火|はっか} is more often spontaneous
- ⟦{点火|てんか}→点火：16200_tenka⟧: lighting a fire — deliberately setting fire to something (a stove, fireworks, etc.)
- ⟦{出火|しゅっか}→出火：20260_shukka⟧: outbreak of fire — the start of a fire as an incident, used in fire investigations
- ⟦{火災|かさい}→火災：02561_kasai⟧: fire (as a disaster) — the resulting fire event, not the moment of ignition
